entry.evidence: It was interpreted as being the detachment between the Lower Allochthon and the autochthonous basement, i.e. the main Caledonian décollement.

steps.action: The authors state the COSC-2 scientific targets: the main décollement and basement deformation, the origin of the deep basement reflectors, palaeoenvironment, palaeoclimate, hydrogeology and heat flow, and deep microbiology.
steps.quote: The origin and nature of the prominent, deep basement reflectors imaged in the seismic profiles

steps.action: From earlier site investigations, the ca. 1200–1250 m continuous reflection is taken as the main décollement hosted in Alum Shale; the magnetotelluric survey instead predicted Alum Shale at ca. 750 m.
steps.quote: It was interpreted as being the detachment between the Lower Allochthon and the autochthonous basement, i.e. the main Caledonian décollement.

steps.action: The authors derive an expected geological section: greywackes, Alum Shale at ca. 750 m, an imbricate system down to the décollement at ca. 1250 m, thin Vemdalen Quartzite, then Rätan granite.
steps.quote: penetrate the shallowest occurrence of Alum Shale at ca. 750 m

steps.action: Rival explanations are stated for the basement: Rätan granite expected from magnetic data, Dala Porphyries possible but unlikely, and the 1.5–2.0 km reflectors as fault zones, dolerites, or both.
steps.quote: which were interpreted to either be (1) major fault zones of yet unknown, but possibly Caledonian age, (2) dolerite intrusions

steps.action: The drill site is chosen from the seismic and magnetotelluric interpretation, and a stopping rule is set: drill until the rocks beneath the basement reflectors are identified.
steps.quote: Drilling would stop, and the borehole would be completed once the nature of the basement rocks beneath these reflections was established.

steps.action: COSC-2A was fully cored to 2276 m (HQ3, then NQ3, then NQ double tube) and COSC-2B to 116 m, with core recovery close to 100 %.
steps.quote: Total core recovery was slightly higher than the total cored length.

steps.action: Under COVID-19 the authors continued drilling with a curtailed, Sweden-based on-site programme: core description postponed to the repository and gas monitoring cancelled.
steps.quote: The latter option was chosen, as the risk of a prolonged delay due to the then-unknown development of the pandemic was judged higher

steps.action: A contamination-controlled microbiology sampling protocol was built: 50 core samples at 50 m intervals, flame sterilisation, a fluorescent microsphere tracer, drilling-fluid reference samples, CARD-FISH fixation and frozen storage.
steps.quote: The surface of the core was flamed to combust contaminating nucleic acids from microbes present in the drilling fluid.

steps.action: Surface decontamination was checked by counting tracer beads on core-surface fragments, and sterilisation was repeated until at least 99.9 % of the beads were quenched.
steps.quote: Flame sterilisation of the core surface was repeated until at least 99.9 % of the microspheres in the drilling liquid had been quenched

steps.action: Because the beads adhered to clay in the drilling fluid, bead addition stopped below 700 m and cores were instead submersed in a bead suspension before decontamination.
steps.quote: As an alternative decontamination control procedure, the microbiology core was, immediately after retrieval, submersed in a liquid containing the fluorescent microspheres

steps.action: The new mDIS drilling information system was used for on-site data acquisition, and the authors report it ready for production workflows.
steps.quote: COSC-2 could demonstrate that this software is ready for production workflows after 2 years of development

steps.action: The core lithologies were described: greywackes to ca. 780 m, sheared black shale over ca. 45 m, sandstones and conglomerates to ca. 1250 m, then porphyries and ignimbrites to TD with dolerites at 1600–1930 m.
steps.quote: At this depth, ignimbrites and volcanic porphyries were encountered for the first time in the borehole (Fig. 4d).

steps.action: The black shale encountered at ca. 780 m is compared with the magnetotelluric prediction and found to agree with it.
steps.quote: which is in accordance with the magnetotelluric site investigations

steps.action: A full downhole logging suite was run (caliper, temperature, susceptibility, resistivity, spectral gamma, sonic, televiewer, gyro); a gamma depth master log was set and core depths were matched to televiewer images in Corelyzer.
steps.quote: the following downhole measurements cover the entire, or at least the open (uncased), part of the borehole

steps.action: The borehole path from the north-seeking gyro was compared with the televiewer orientation sensors (HiRAT, Abi43) to qualify televiewer imagery for core orientation.
steps.quote: The gyro and televiewer orientation match closely (Fig. 5) but with a slightly higher deviation of the Abi43.

steps.action: The expected geological section is compared with the drilled section, both overlain on the depth-converted seismic section.
steps.quote: Comparing the expected geological section with the drilled section (Fig. 2) allows a number of observations.

steps.action: The authors reject the imbricate-system interpretation and the 1250 m reflection as the décollement; the Alum Shale sits in its original stratigraphic position and the reflection marks the top of the Dala Porphyries.
steps.quote: is not related to the main Caledonian décollement but to the top of the Dala Porphyries

steps.action: The claim is revised: the main detachment is placed in the less-strained-than-expected Alum Shale at ca. 780–825 m.
steps.quote: we regard it as being the main detachment horizon that occurs a level of ca. 780–825 m

steps.action: The expected thin Neoproterozoic quartzite is replaced by a much thicker sedimentary basement cover, interpreted from its turbiditic background as deposited in the initial stages of the Paleozoic basin.
steps.quote: the turbiditic background sedimentation in this depth interval of COSC-2 suggests that the deposition of these coarse siliciclastics happened during the initial stages

steps.action: Among the reflector rivals, the dolerite interpretation is kept: the 1.5–2 km reflections correspond to dolerites with some marginal deformation.
steps.quote: the prominent reflections between ∼ 1.5 and 2 km correspond, as expected, to dolerites

steps.action: Rätan granite was not encountered, so the auxiliary is revised: the granite causing the regional magnetic anomaly is placed at greater depth.
steps.quote: the Rätan-type granite that is responsible for the regional magnetic anomaly is now expected to be located at greater depth

steps.action: Frequent slumping and dewatering structures are proposed to be a common feature of the Early Paleozoic margin of Baltica.
steps.quote: [...] and dewatering structures) frequently disturbs the Palaeozoic section of the drill core

steps.action: A preliminary synthetic seismogram was computed from the P-wave sonic log (constant density, Gaussian-derivative wavelet, 80 Hz maximum frequency).
steps.quote: The P-wave sonic log (Fig. 6) was used as input for generating a preliminary synthetic seismogram

steps.action: The synthetic seismogram is compared with the surface seismic section: Alum Shale (0.32 s), top of the porphyries (0.48 s) and the dolerite top and base tie to reflections.
steps.quote: Good correlation is observed between the synthetic seismogram and the surface data (Fig. 7).

steps.action: The authors state that the target of understanding basement seismic reflectivity has been addressed from the downhole logs and the preliminary core assessment.
steps.quote: the project successfully addressed the target of understanding the seismic reflectivity in the basement

tree.answer: Yes: an orogen-scale décollement and deep basement reflectors imaged by seismics
Not before drilling (inferred from seismic/MT); directly sampled by continuous coring
Test the expected section and identify the reflector sources
Yes: décollement at 1250 m vs Alum Shale at 750 m; reflectors as faults, dolerites or both; granite vs porphyry
Yes: the rivals predict different lithologies at depth in the core
Found: one borehole at a chosen site

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: No repetition by nature; a single site, set beside COSC-1 and outcrop
Partly: synthetic-seismogram tie and gyro–televiewer cross-check; no independent replication
Expected décollement depth and imbricate model rejected; dolerite reflectors kept

end.claim: Drilling shows the main Caledonian décollement lies in the Alum Shale at ca. 780–825 m, not at the expected ca. 1250 m, where the continuous reflection marks the top of the Dala Porphyries.

decisive_move.sentence: Continuous coring to 2276 m, which recovered Alum Shale at ca. 780 m and porphyries from ca. 1250 m, is the step without which the revised décollement depth and the reinterpreted 1250 m reflector would not exist.

gates.evidence: The site and stopping rule were set from the seismic/MT interpretation (§2 ¶1, §2.2 ¶1), and that expected section could have been confirmed by the core but failed for décollement depth and basement rock type (§5 ¶2). The expectation was published beforehand (Juhlin et al., 2016), but no comparison criteria or analysis were fixed before the data.

imports.item: Fluorescent microsphere tracer for drilling contamination control (Friese et al., 2017)
CARD-FISH (fluorescence in situ hybridisation with catalysed reporter deposition)
Sequencing of ribosomal RNA marker genes and genomic reconstruction (planned)
OGC borehole interoperability reference systems (Grellet et al., 2020)

novelty_claims.quote: As the first major scientific drilling project that used the new mDIS software for the acquisition of [...]
the scientific community now has access to a nearly continuous composite geological section (outcrop and COSC-1 and COSC-2 drill cores)

limits: This is a preliminary science report. The detailed core description was postponed and is not reported. Targets 3–6 (palaeoenvironment, palaeoclimate, hydrogeology, microbiology) are only planned, so the drilling-fluid contaminant controls were collected but not yet analysed. Sub-claim statuses: core recovery, the microbiology protocols and mDIS are capability_characterized; dolerites as reflector source is best_explanation; Rätan granite at greater depth is an untested protective inference; synsedimentary deformation as a margin-wide feature is a conjecture. The synthetic seismogram rests on constant density and one wavelet, with no alternatives reported. Composition is none_fits: an expected section was frozen before drilling and tested by direct sampling, which is close to forecast_verification, but there is no scoring against a reference and much of the report is operational. Inference: how much of the expected section was fixed before drilling beyond Juhlin et al. (2016), and whether the post-drilling interpretation changed during review, is not shown. No review file was supplied.

disagreements.target: Site-investigation interpretation (Juhlin et al., 2016) of the ca. 1250 m reflection as the main Caledonian décollement
disagreements.support: The core shows porphyry basement at ca. 1250 m and sheared Alum Shale at ca. 800 m in its original stratigraphic position, and the synthetic seismogram ties the reflection to the top of the porphyries.
disagreements.quote: is not related to the main Caledonian décollement but to the top of the Dala Porphyries

disagreements.target: Imbricate-system interpretation of the 750–1250 m interval from site investigations
disagreements.support: The Alum Shale lies in stratigraphic position above a thick clastic cover rather than being imbricated upwards from the décollement.
disagreements.quote: this shale was not transported upwards from the décollement at about 1250 m in an imbricate system, as interpreted from site investigations

disagreements.target: Former interpretations (Dyrelius, 1980) placing Rätan granite beneath the COSC area
disagreements.support: The borehole found weakly magnetic Dala Porphyries to at least 2.3 km and no Rätan granite.
disagreements.quote: In contrast to former interpretations, the Rätan-type granite that is responsible for the regional magnetic anomaly is now expected to be located at greater depth.

disagreements.target: Thin sedimentary basement cover along the Caledonian front (Andersson et al., 1985; Juhlin et al., 2016)
disagreements.support: The core shows ca. 425 m of coarse clastic cover between the Alum Shale and the basement.
disagreements.quote: The latter is usually only up to some tens of metres thick and of Neoproterozoic age along [...]
